Header: Chilo infuscatellus Vernacular name: Illam kuruthu Puzhu.

Prevention: Planting to be done in early season (Dec – Jan)
Avoid moisture stress in the early stages of crop, e.g. by making small bundles of plant trash and put them in furrows.
Intercropping with dhaincha or pulses to repel the adults.
Monitoring: Presence of egg masses under the surface of the leaves.
Presence of dead hearts which can be easily pulled out.
Presence of bore holes at the collar region.
Light trap catches @ one per five hectare.
Monitoring through pheromone traps @ 5 per acre.
Erect the trap at 15 days after planting. (Replace the septa once every three weeks.)
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Virus (750 numbers of diseased larvae) 200ml per acre.
Trichogramma chilonis 2cc per acre /release for three times at fifteen days interval starting from 30 days after planting.
Sturmiopsis inferens /ha on 30 and 45 days after planting.
Spray neem seed kernel extract 5%. (25 kg of
NSK/ha dissolved in 500 litres of water).
Direct Control (Chemical): Repeated use of same insecticide should be avoided.
Avoid spraying insecticides up to five to seven days after parasitoid release.
Spray chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 375 ml per ha.
Spray fipronil 5% SC @ 2 litres per ha.
Spray quinalphos 25% EC 2 litres per ha.
Restrictions: U (Unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use).
